subject: Post-call recap: Acme ML Assistant — model + eval plan, schema & callable tools
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <trivera@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme ML Assistant — model + eval plan, schema & callable tools

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we all have the same playbook.

Highlights from the call:
- Primary goal: replace rule-based response generation in Acme Support Assistant with an LLM-backed workflow that emits structured JSON and triggers internal tools (ticket.create, user.lookup).
- Constraints: deployment must be within Acme VPC (private deployment), latency SLO ~ <300ms p95 for single-threaded flows, volume ~ 5k concurrent users peak, strict audit logging and retention for 12 months.
- Quality target: extraction-fields F1 >= 0.92 on your holdout test set; tolerable hallucination rate <2% on named entities.
- Cost sensitivity: pilot budget target ~$Xk/month; willing to evaluate quantized model variants.

Our immediate proposal:
1) Redwood runs a focused model-fit + structured-output eval using your sample prompts & 200 labelled examples you provide. Deliverables: benchmark summary, per-model JSON-schema compliance rates, suggested model/quantization profiles.
2) Tests will include function-calling simulations and an eval harness to exercise retries/fallbacks and partial-output handling. We'll run: Redwood-7B-Chat-q8, Llama-2-13B-chat (q4_0), Mistral-Instruct-7B (q8_0) as starting variants; we can add smaller distilled candidates if latency/cost needs push.
3) We will validate JSON schema adherence (strict vs. lenient modes) and simulate failure modes: truncated outputs, schema violations, and tool-calling idempotency.
4) Timeline: initial results and a short readout by EOD next Thu (2026-05-27).

Immediate asks for you: please confirm (a) sample prompts/dataset availability (b) whether the function endpoints can be hit from a private test harness (we can also run a mock), and (c) whether someone from your security team can join the review for audit requirements.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt seeds), acme_json_schema_v2.json (schema draft) — I attached stubs to the thread.

If this looks right I’ll assign owners and kick off the eval. Suggested 30-min follow-up next Tue to review benchmarks.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(karthik.iyer@redwood.com)

From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Rivera <trivera@acme.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme ML Assistant — model + eval plan, schema & callable tools

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) JSON schema: the attached acme_json_schema_v2.json is our canonical schema. Two fields we care about: customer_id (string, must be a valid UUID) and action.intent (enum: [create_ticket, escalate, provide_info]). How strict are your "strict vs lenient" modes — will Redwood reject responses that don't validate, or return them with an error wrapper so we can decide?

2) Retries & idempotency: when a function call fails and the model retries, do you have tooling to ensure duplicate ticket.create isn't issued? We want idempotent behavior for the ticket API.

3) Audit logs: we need proof of retention and tamper-resistance for the trial. Tom will loop in our security lead (Maya).

Attachments: acme_json_schema_v2.json (attached)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: Acme ML Assistant — model + eval plan, schema & callable tools

Hi Alice — quick note from the evaluation side with concrete test plan and links.

What we'll run (first pass):
- Data: your 200 labelled examples + 800 synthetic prompt variations (to exercise entity permutations).
- Models & configs: Redwood-7B-Chat (q8_0), Llama-2-13B-chat (q4_0), Mistral-Instruct-7B (q8_0). Each candidate will be evaluated in "strict-validator" and "lenient-accept" modes for schema compliance.
- Function-calling tests: simulate success, transient failure (HTTP 502), and consistent failure (400). For transient failures we'll test retry policies: immediate retry up to 2 attempts with exponential backoff and an idempotency token. For ticket.create we'll assert Redwood's mock harness issues idempotency-token headers and verifies no duplicate creates.
- Structured output checks: validate JSON against acme_json_schema_v2.json. Metrics: schema_valid_rate, field_precision/recall, partial_output_rate, average token cost.

Deliverables (one consolidated PDF + CSV per model): benchmark summary (redwood_benchmark_summary_MAY2026.pdf), raw eval CSVs, annotated examples where models diverged, and a short readout deck. All artifacts will be uploaded to the Google Drive link below.

Light technical notes:
- When model returns malformed JSON we will attempt two repair passes (heuristic closing braces + guided completion) and then mark as "repair-failed" for strict mode. For tool-calls, the harness will surface the full model response so you can choose to accept repaired output or not.
- Fallbacks: failing candidate -> drop to smaller Redwood-7B with cached KV prefixes to maintain latency. We will record fallback frequency as part of SLO analysis.

Links & artifacts:
- Drive folder (read-only for your team): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxyz/acme-evals
- Benchmark run: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/acme-ACME-2026-089
- HubSpot deal: HS-98765

Attachments included in kickoff: acme_prompt_set_v1.txt, acme_json_schema_v2.json (you already attached), redwood_benchmark_summary_MAY2026.pdf (initial template).

We can also run the test harness inside an Acme test subnet if you prefer — that eliminates VPC egress concerns. Let me know and we’ll coordinate infra.

—Marissa
Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Rivera <trivera@acme.com>

Appreciate the detail — a few follow-ups from the security and procurement side:

- Can you confirm the exact idempotency tokens and headers your harness will add to ticket.create requests? We need to make sure they match our ticketing API (X-Acme-Idempotency).
- Audit logs: can you provide a sample retention policy and the cryptographic integrity guarantees (or where in the Private deployment docs we can find tamper-resistance details)? Our security team needs this for procurement.
- Timeline: procurement has a review window next Monday; if Redwood can provide the SOC2 artifact and a short security summary by EOD Monday we can move forward with a PO.

Attaching our security questionnaire (acme_security_questionnaire.docx) for completeness. Maya will join the readout next week.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Support Platforms — Acme

2) Acme: confirm whether we'd like the harness to run inside your test subnet or via a Redwood mock (Owner: Alice) — please confirm by Tue 2026-05-25.
